newsitem.title: USA: American Restaurant may cut distributions.
newsitem.headline: American Restaurant may cut distributions.

text.p: American Restaurant Partners Lp said Thursday it may reduce cash distributions if it begins paying income taxes next year.

"As we have previously reported, the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1987 provides that publicly traded limited partnerships will become taxable entities beginning in 1998. Without some change in organizational structure, our company will start paying income taxes at the company level as of January 1, 1998. This would decrease the amount of cash available to the company by the amount of taxes it must pay. As a result the company would have to reduce cash distributions by the amount of the taxes. We are carefully weighing all options available to us to ensure the long-term viability of the company," Hal McCoy, chairman of the managing general partner, said in a statement.

Earlier this month American Restaurant reduced its quarterly cash distribution to its Class A income preference unit holders to $0.05 a unit from $0.06 paid in January and April. The reduction was due to poor operating results this year, McCoy said.
